ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in the Cartesian coordinate system, A(8, 0), point B is a moving point on the graph of the linear function $y=x$. Taking OB as a side, a square OBCD is constructed. When AB is at its minimum length, point D just falls on the graph of the inverse proportion function $y=\frac{k}{x}$. Then, $k=$ (\quad)
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} According to the principle that a perpendicular line segment is the shortest, when AB is perpendicular to the line $y=x$, AB is at its shortest,\\
$\because$ $\angle AOB=45^\circ$\\
$\therefore$ $\angle BAO=45^\circ$\\
$\therefore$ $\triangle AOB$ is an isosceles right triangle,\\
$\because$ the coordinates of point A are (8, 0)\\
$\therefore$ OA=8\\
$\therefore$ $BO=BA=4\sqrt{2}$\\
$\because$ quadrilateral OBCD is a square,\\
$\therefore$ $DO=BO=4\sqrt{2}$, $\angle DOB=90^\circ$\\
$\therefore$ $\angle DOC=\angle BOC=45^\circ$\\
Draw DE$\perp$x-axis through point D at point E,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle ODE=\angle DOE=45^\circ$\\
$\therefore$ $\triangle DEO$ is an isosceles right triangle,\\
$\therefore$ $DE=OE=\frac{DO}{\sqrt{2}}=\frac{4\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{2}}=4$\\
$\because$ point D is in the second quadrant,\\
$\therefore$ D(−4, 4)\\
Also, point D is on the graph of the reciprocal function $y=\frac{k}{x}$\\
$\therefore$ $k=(−4)\times 4=\boxed{-16}$

solver_metadata.cot_raw: 图像描述：图中是直角坐标系，O 为原点，A 在 x 轴正方向上；B 位于过原点的斜线 y=x 上；线段 AB 从 A 连到 B；以 OB 为一边作正方形 OBCD，图中 D 位于 O 的左上方，即第二象限方向，C 在 y 轴附近上方。推理：当点 A 到直线 y=x 上的动点 B 的距离 AB 最小时，AB 应垂直于直线 y=x，也就是 AB⊥OB。直线 y=x 与 x 轴夹角为 45°，所以 ∠AOB=45°。又因为 AB⊥OB，所以三角形 AOB 是 45°-45°-90°直角三角形，OA 是斜边。A=(8,0)，因此 OA=8，故 OB=8/√2=4√2。正方形 OBCD 中 OD=OB=4√2，且 OD 垂直于 OB。按图中方向，OD 指向第二象限，方向角为 135°，所以 D 的坐标为 (4√2 cos135°, 4√2 sin135°)=(-4,4)。点 D 在反比例函数 y=k/x 上，因此 k=xy=(-4)×4=-16。

raw_record.original_question: As shown in the figure, in the Cartesian coordinate system, A(8, 0), point B is a moving point on the graph of the linear function $y=x$. Taking OB as a side, a square OBCD is constructed. When AB is at its minimum length, point D just falls on the graph of the inverse proportion function $y=\frac{k}{x}$. Then, $k=$ (\quad)
raw_record.answer:
\textbf{Solution:} According to the principle that a perpendicular line segment is the shortest, when AB is perpendicular to the line $y=x$, AB is at its shortest,\\
$\because$ $\angle AOB=45^\circ$\\
$\therefore$ $\angle BAO=45^\circ$\\
$\therefore$ $\triangle AOB$ is an isosceles right triangle,\\
$\because$ the coordinates of point A are (8, 0)\\
$\therefore$ OA=8\\
$\therefore$ $BO=BA=4\sqrt{2}$\\
$\because$ quadrilateral OBCD is a square,\\
$\therefore$ $DO=BO=4\sqrt{2}$, $\angle DOB=90^\circ$\\
$\therefore$ $\angle DOC=\angle BOC=45^\circ$\\
Draw DE$\perp$x-axis through point D at point E,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle ODE=\angle DOE=45^\circ$\\
$\therefore$ $\triangle DEO$ is an isosceles right triangle,\\
$\therefore$ $DE=OE=\frac{DO}{\sqrt{2}}=\frac{4\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{2}}=4$\\
$\because$ point D is in the second quadrant,\\
$\therefore$ D(-4, 4)\\
Also, point D is on the graph of the reciprocal function $y=\frac{k}{x}$\\
$\therefore$ $k=(-4)\times 4=\boxed{-16}$
raw_record.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure, the coordinate axes intersect at O, and A is marked on the positive x-axis; B is located on the oblique straight line y=x in the first quadrant; a square OBCD is constructed with OB as a side, and the square is drawn on the left side of OB, so point D is located in the second quadrant. Then reason: Let B=(t,t). Because B is on y=x, and the figure shows B in the first quadrant, t>0. A=(8,0), so AB^2=(t-8)^2+(t-0)^2=(t-8)^2+t^2=2t^2-16t+64=2(t-4)^2+32. When t=4, AB^2 is minimum, that is, AB is minimum; at this time B=(4,4). From the direction of the square in the figure, D is the endpoint obtained by rotating the vector OB=(4,4) counterclockwise 90° about O, so OD=(-4,4), that is, D=(-4,4). Point D is on the inverse proportional function y=k/x, so k=xy=(-4)×4=-16.
